locator.section: 8.4/8.5 charge-remote fragmentation; the 'classic example (Adams and Gross 1989)' using FAB (Li+) ionization of an unsaturated fatty acid

evidence.curator_note: Charge-remote fragmentation (CRF) of a FAB-generated, doubly-lithiated unsaturated-fatty-acid cation (Adams and Gross 1989). The reacting site is REMOTE from the charge: the whole point of the scheme (and the surrounding text, 'By stabilizing the charge at a remote site, isomerization can be minimized to give location-specific decompositions') is that the dilithio-carboxyl carbenium (map 9, [C+](OLi)(OLi)) is a spectator - it carries the charge but does not participate in any electron move. NET REACTION (curator's conserving reconstruction; see DRAWING DEFICIENCY below): R-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH=CH-(CH2)n-C(OLi)2+  ->  R-CH=CH2  +  H2  +  CH2=CH-CH=CH-(CH2)n-C(OLi)2+ . A single C-C bond (the homoallylic Cb-Cc bond, maps 3-4) is cleaved, H2 is eliminated, and two olefinic termini are created; the charged fragment is encoded as the conjugated 1,3-diene CH2=CH-CH=CH-(CH2)n-C(OLi)2+ (a new C=C at map 4=5 plus the map 6=7 C=C), the mass-conserving, location-specific CRF product. ARC COUNT (convention D): the book draws 0 (zero) curved arrows/fishhooks - Equation 8.36 is a net reactant->products scheme, not an arrow-pushing diagram. What the figure DOES draw explicitly are the individual hydrogens: the two bracket carbons that lose an H are drawn with a single H on top (RCH, map 2; and the apex CH, map 5), while the two carbons that keep both H and become the =CH2 termini are drawn 'H2C'/'CH2' (maps 3 and 4). That explicit-H drawing is the book's only mechanistic hint. The two departing hydrogens are encoded as protium-1 isotope labels ([1H:20] on Ca, [1H:21] on Cd) so they remain explicit, map-stable atoms that RDKit does not fold into implicit-H counts (the house convention used e.g. in IMS4-EQ4.37); the mass number 1 is ordinary protium, so no mass is altered. All 3 encoded electron_moves are therefore IMPLICIT (electron flow reconstructed for balance; not drawn on the page): move <1> routes the Ca-Ha bonding pair (bond 2-20) into the forming H-H bond (bond 20-21); move <2> routes the Cd-Hd bonding pair (bond 5-21) into the forming Cc=Cd pi bond (bond 4-5); move <3> routes the cleaving Cb-Cc sigma pair (bond 3-4) into the forming Ca=Cb pi bond (bond 2-3). This closed-shell 6-centre (Ha-Ca-Cb-Cc-Cd-Hd) concerted 1,4-elimination of H2 with allylic C-C cleavage keeps every species even-electron (EE+ throughout, no radicals) - consistent with the charge/radical NOT being localized at the reacting site. CRF mechanism is debated (concerted 1,4-H2 elimination vs. stepwise homolytic radical pathway); the concerted closed-shell version is encoded because the page shows neither arrows nor radicals and the ion is a closed-shell FAB adduct. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the book scheme is generic (R and n are undefined and NO m/z or intensity is printed). It is instantiated here as R = CH3 and n = 1, giving precursor C9H15Li2O2+ (curator-computed m/z 169.138) -> propene (R-CH=CH2) + H2 + the C6H7Li2O2+ diene cation (curator-computed m/z 125.076). These m/z are products of the chosen instantiation, NOT measurements from the book. LOCALIZATION (conventions B/C): the remote carboxyl cation is drawn as a delocalized/resonance dilithio-carboxylate carbenium (one C-O drawn as a partial double bond, the other dashed, with a '+'); it is written here in the single localized form [C+](OLi)(OLi) with both C-O single and the '+' on carbon - the exact bonds do not affect the (spectator) electron bookkeeping. DRAWING DEFICIENCY (pixel-verified, convention D): the book DRAWS the charged product as a MONO-ene (only the terminal vinyl H2C=CH-; the two mid-chain CH's are joined by a SINGLE bond, no '=', unlike the precursor's crisply-drawn 'CH=CH'), so as literally drawn the charged fragment is one CH short of and mass-imbalanced with the precursor -- a book drawing imprecision. The conjugated 1,3-diene encoded here is the curator's mass-conserving CORRECTION, NOT a literal transcription of the figure.

NO MOD rule is assigned to Equation 8.36 (rule_index.json 'by_equation' has entries only up to 8.14; there is no 8.36 key, and n_equations = 57). No cross-link is asserted. Chapter 8's MOD rules (IMS_8_*) encode radical-site and charge-site alpha/inductive/rH/rd fragmentations of small closed-shell or radical-cation ions; none encode a charge-remote 1,4-H2 elimination with allylic C-C cleavage of a lithiated fatty-acid cation, and the generic R/n chain here has no fixed-topology rule pattern to match against. All m/z quoted (precursor 169.138 for C9H15Li2O2+, product 125.076 for C6H7Li2O2+, neutral losses propene 42.047 and H2 2.016) are curator-computed from the transcribed R=CH3, n=1 instantiation because the page prints no m/z and no intensity.
